Covariance Matrix for a Distance-Removal Model with a Fixed-Range Field

Source: R/gdr_response_field_covariance.R
vcov-unmarkedFitGDRField-method.Rd

Return the covariance matrix of the coefficients of a model fitted by fit_gdr_response_field(). The matrix is retained from the fit, so this method does not rerun TMB. It matches coef() on the link scale and keeps the covariances between components and between the fixed coefficients and the field values.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'unmarkedFitGDRField'
vcov(object, type, altNames = TRUE, method = "hessian", fixedOnly = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

object

An unmarkedFitGDRField returned by fit_gdr_response_field().

type

Optional character naming one component: "lambda" (abundance), "dist" (distance) or "rem" (removal). If omitted, all components are returned together, in the order of coef(object).

altNames

Logical, default TRUE. TRUE labels rows and columns with component prefixes, such as lambda(Int), as coef() does.

method

Character. Only "hessian", the default, is available. It returns the covariance computed from the curvature of the likelihood during fitting. Bootstrap covariance is not available for this model.

fixedOnly

Logical, default TRUE. TRUE returns the fixed regression coefficients only. FALSE adds the field value of every block (labeled lambda(b_lambda)) and any observer intercepts in the distance component.

...

Not used. Unrecognized arguments stop the call.

Value

A square numeric matrix with row and column names matching coef(object, type, altNames = altNames, fixedOnly = fixedOnly). Entries are on the link scale of each coefficient: log for abundance and distance, logit for removal. Block field values are physical deviations on the log density scale, not TMB's internal whitened values. The square roots of the diagonal are the standard errors.

Details

The log SDs of the random effects are estimated parameters, but they are not rows of this matrix. Use unmarked::sigma(object) to see the field SD with its confidence limits.

The matrix treats the ecological scales of effect and the correlation range as known, and it contains no observation noise. confint() uses it for normal (Wald) intervals, and predict() uses it for standard errors.

See also

fit_gdr_response_field(), unmarkedFitGDRField, predict,unmarkedFitGDRField-method

Examples

# \donttest{
# The field needs unmarked 1.5.2 and TMB 1.9.25.
if (requireNamespace("TMB", quietly = TRUE) &&
    utils::packageVersion("unmarked") == "1.5.2" &&
    utils::packageVersion("TMB") == "1.9.25") {
  # Eight survey blocks 1 km apart, six point counts in each
  block <- factor(rep(paste0("b", 1:8), each = 6))
  hab <- rep(seq(-1, 1, length.out = 6), 8)
  shift <- c(-0.4, -0.3, -0.1, 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.35, 0.4)[block]
  sim <- sim_dat_gdr(density = exp(log(400) + 0.5 * hab + shift),
    distance_scale = 40, removal = 0.2, dist_breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75),
    interval_lengths = c(2, 3, 5), interval_units = "minutes",
    site_covs = data.frame(hab = hab, block = block), seed = 1)
  template <- unmarked::gdistremoval(lambdaformula = ~ hab + (1 | block),
    removalformula = ~ 1, distanceformula = ~ 1, data = sim$observed,
    keyfun = "halfnorm", mixture = "P", output = "density",
    unitsOut = "kmsq", K = 60, engine = "TMB",
    starts = c(log(400), 0, log(40), qlogis(0.2), log(0.3)))
  block_xy <- cbind(x = 500000 + 1000 * (as.integer(block) - 1),
                    y = 4400000)
  rownames(block_xy) <- rownames(unmarked::siteCovs(sim$observed))
  cold <- c("beta_lambda[1]" = log(300), "beta_lambda[2]" = 0,
            "beta_dist[1]" = log(30), "beta_rem[1]" = qlogis(0.4),
            "lsigma_lambda[1]" = log(0.5))
  settings <- list(method = "BFGS", se = TRUE, threads = 1L,
                   control = list(maxit = 2500L, reltol = 1e-10))
  field_fit <- fit_gdr_response_field(template, block_xy, crs = 32617,
    range = 2000, cold_starts = list(cold = cold),
    audit_dir = tempfile("gdr-field-"), tmb_settings = settings)

  # Abundance coefficients: covariance and standard errors (log scale)
  V <- vcov(field_fit, type = "lambda")
  print(V)
  print(sqrt(diag(V)))
  # All components together: abundance, distance, then removal
  print(round(vcov(field_fit), 4))
  # Adding the eight block field values gives a 10 x 10 matrix
  print(dim(vcov(field_fit, type = "lambda", fixedOnly = FALSE)))
}
#>             lambda(Int) lambda(hab)
#> lambda(Int)  0.04813091 -0.00292675
#> lambda(hab) -0.00292675  0.01444965
#> lambda(Int) lambda(hab) 
#>   0.2193876   0.1202067 
#>             lambda(Int) lambda(hab) dist(Int) rem(Int)
#> lambda(Int)      0.0481     -0.0029   -0.0104  -0.0126
#> lambda(hab)     -0.0029      0.0144    0.0000   0.0000
#> dist(Int)       -0.0104      0.0000    0.0079   0.0000
#> rem(Int)        -0.0126      0.0000    0.0000   0.0384
#> [1] 10 10
# }
